key_insight: Patch-aligned features from foundation models (e.g., BLIP2) are highly redundant (≈90% redundancy), and training end-to-end driving policies on a stochastically selected subset of patches reduces redundancy and improves Out-of-Distribution generalization.
problem_solved: Reduces redundancy and over-reliance on correlated patch features in foundation-model representations to improve robustness and generalization of end-to-end autonomous driving policies under OOD conditions.
method: Measure redundancy in foundation-model patch features using PCA (variance explained) and cross-patch similarity analysis.
Apply stochastic patch selection: randomly sample a subset of patch features during training to break redundancy and force diverse, informative representations.
Train end-to-end driving policies on the reduced/stochastic patch set and evaluate OOD generalization and efficiency.
impact: Improves robustness and OOD generalization for vision-to-control systems while reducing input redundancy and computational load—beneficial for practitioners building reliable, efficient autonomous-driving models.
visual_elements: PCA scree/variance-explained plot showing ~90% variance captured by few components (quantifies redundancy).
Cross-patch similarity heatmap to visualize high inter-patch correlation in foundation-model features.
Image-grid diagram showing patches with stochastic selection highlighted across training steps (illustrates method).
Performance bar/line chart comparing in-distribution vs OOD driving metrics and compute/feature count with and without stochastic patch selection.
paper_title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection
paper_authors: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus
